exampleAnswers.title: Identifying Infinite Limits when the Left and Right Limits are the Same

question.text: The figure above shows the graph of $f(x).$ Therefore
question.explanation:
We see from the graph that as $x$ approaches $1$ from the left, the function $f(x)$ approaches $-\infty.$ So, the left-hand limit is

\[ \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 1^-} f(x) = -\infty \, . \]

Likewise, as $x$ approaches $1$ from the right, the function $f(x)$ again approaches $-\infty.$ So, the right-hand limit is

\[ \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 1^+} f(x) = -\infty \, . \]

Consequently,

\[ \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 1} f(x)=-\infty \, . \]

question.text:
Which of the following statements are true concerning the function $y=f(x) $ whose graph is shown above?

  1. $\lim_\limits{x\to 3^+} f(x) = \infty$
  2. $\lim_\limits{x\to 3^-} f(x)= \infty$
  3. $\lim_\limits{x\to 3} f(x)= 1$
question.explanation:
First, let's compute the limits in question.

We see from the graph that as $x$ approaches $3$ from the left, the function $f(x)$ approaches $\infty.$ So, the left-hand limit is

\[ \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 3^-} f(x) = \infty \, . \]

Likewise, as $x$ approaches $3$ from the right, the function $f(x)$ again approaches $\infty.$ So, the right-hand limit is

\[ \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 3^+} f(x) = \infty \, . \]

Consequently,

\[ \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 3} f(x)=\infty \, . \]

Now, let's examine each statement in turn.

  • Statement I is true.

  • Statement II is true.

  • Statement III is false.

In conclusion, statements I and II are true.

exampleAnswers.title: Identifying Infinite Limits when the Left and Right Limits are Different

question.text:
Which of the following statements are true concerning the function $y=f(x) $ whose graph is shown above?

  1. $\lim_\limits{x\to 1^+} f(x) = -\infty$
  2. $\lim_\limits{x\to 1^-} f(x)= -\infty$
  3. $\lim_\limits{x\to 1} f(x)= \text{DNE}$
question.explanation:
First, let's compute the limits in question.

As $x$ approaches $1$ from the right, the function value $f(x)$ goes to $-\infty,$ and therefore

\[ \lim_\limits{x\to 1^+} f(x)=-\infty. \]

As $x$ approaches $1$ from the left, the function is not defined. So we have \[ \lim_\limits{x\to 1^-} f(x)=\text{DNE}. \]

Therefore,

\[ \lim_\limits{x\to 1} f(x)=\text{DNE}. \]

Now, let's examine each statement in turn.

  • Statement I is true.

  • Statement II is false.

  • Statement III is true.

In conclusion, only statements I and III are true.
